correctness.rationale: For even \(m\), Cheng--Wang--Xiang explicitly prove the sharp estimate for arbitrary \(L_1\)-spaces; replacing the finite-dimensional range in Wang's parity-coset proof by \(X=\ell_1(\Gamma)\) preserves every step and gives normalized forward constant \(22\). Wang's quotient-duality theorem then yields pointwise \(\ell_\infty(\Gamma)\)-valued liftings. The closed relation \(R=\{(g,h):Ah=Bg\}\), equipped with \(\max\{\|g\|,\|h\|/22\}\), projects onto the data space with Banach constant exactly \(1\); quantitative Bartle--Graves therefore supplies a continuous positively homogeneous section with arbitrarily small multiplicative loss, and odd symmetrization preserves both the equation and the bound. For odd \(m\), the exact parity witness has zero sign difference but nonzero antipodal difference; Hahn--Banach then gives a datum whose adjoint equation is inconsistent. The endpoint \(p=1\) (so \(p'=\infty\)), arbitrary \(\Gamma\), and the boundary \(n\ge2\) were checked.

value.rationale: The result identifies a sharp structural boundary in the new divergence-lifting problem. On every admissible even scale it upgrades finite-coordinate existence to a single continuous nonlinear selector on arbitrary, potentially nonseparable \(\ell_\infty(\Gamma)\) data with dimension-free control; on every odd scale it shows that solvability itself fails for some datum. This distinguishes a genuine parity obstruction from the weaker phenomenon of large or nonexistent regular linear factorizations and gives a reusable infinite-dimensional selection mechanism at the sharp metric-cotype scale.
